prompt: Two boards meet a square corner post so that their angles are complementary. If one board sits at $35^\circ$, what is the measure of the other angle, in degrees?
hint: The word complementary tells you what the two angles add up to. Which total goes with a square corner?

hints.text: The word complementary tells you what the two angles add up to. Which total goes with a square corner?
Complementary angles have a sum of $90^\circ$, so subtract the known angle from that total: work out $90 - 35$.

explanation: Two angles are complementary when their measures add to $90^\circ$, the size of a square corner.
One angle is $35^\circ$, so the other is what is left of the $90^\circ$: $90 - 35 = 55$.
The check $35 + 55 = 90$ works, so the other angle is $55^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: C comes before S
steps: Complementary comes first in the alphabet and pairs with the smaller total, $90^\circ$ (a Corner).
Supplementary comes later and pairs with $180^\circ$ (a Straight line). Here the corner post makes it $90 - 35 = 55$.
